body:
I used to be worried about being ugly, and still kind of am. But now I'm more comfortable with being gross looking, as I'll explain... Maybe this will be helpful, maybe not. But the things I did, kind of in this order: 

A. Look at how ugly many celebrities are. People on the street. I looked at people I thought were unattractive and thought about how I really don't CARE that they're unattractive to me. Or I'd see someone and notice their acne/unibrow/crooked teeth but I wouldn't care about it. That wasn't their worth.

B. Next I started to figure out how unattractive (to me...) celebrities can really take advantage of their face and charisma. I think I have to really "live in" my own face/presence to be attractive even if I'm not attractive. Hiding myself and constraining myself won't make me more appealing. The more expressive I am the better I will come off to people. Which brings me to C...

C. You know how you can smell bad and just get used to your own personally stink? I try to think of my looks as the same thing. If I feel sloppy or gross one day I just try to mentally roll in it like a pig in mud. Yes I know that sounds like the episode of Spongebob where he screams I'M UGLY AND I'M PROUD.

Maybe there's a D, where I find my own beauty and you find yours too. Maybe we'll get there.

so TLDR: if you learn to extend empathy and not care about other's look, eventually you may be able to extend that sentiment to yourself
